verdict.reasoning: Patient reports shortness of breath for 2–3 days: 'So recently... I have feel like kind of shorter breath.' and when asked duration: '2, 3 days? Yeah, quite recently.'
Same as cc-001; shortness of breath for 2–3 days described as a recent issue, consistent with worsening: '2, 3 days? Yeah, quite recently.'
Patient reports cough along with shortness of breath: 'I have cough and coughlot and I have a fever. I also used to walk to work, but recently I can't because... I feel like very short of breath.'

Patient initially says 'I have a fever' but then clarifies normal measured temperature: 'Did you say you checked your temperature already?' 'Yes, I checked.' 'Was it normal?' 'Yeah, yeah.' 'What was your temperature?' '37. Yeah.' This contradicts describing it as a subjective fever associated with SOB.

Patient notes difficulty finishing sentences when symptomatic: 'I feel like very short of breath and sometimes I feel like I can't even finish top saying a sentence. It's quite difficult to... complete the... talking sometimes.' This occurs with walking/effort.

Exercise intolerance is indicated by inability to walk to work and do exercise: 'I also used to walk to work, but recently I can't because... I feel like very short of breath' and later 'Have you been able to do any exercise?' 'No, I can't.'
Daytime exertional dyspnea: 'Just daytime walking? Yeah.' and 'Just walk or. Sometimes, but currently I feel. I feel.' in response to when short of breath.
Explicit denial of chest pain: 'And any chest pain?' 'No chest pain? No.'
No nocturnal wakening: 'Have you been woken up at night time at all?' 'No. Just daytime walking? Yeah.'
No sputum: 'Have you coughed any phlegm up or anything like that?' 'No.'
No haemoptysis: 'Any, any blood in there when you cough?' 'No, I don't think so.'

History of asthma as a child and also in adulthood: when asked about childhood wheeze/asthma: 'Yes, I had asthma.' Asked if similar symptoms as adult: 'Sorry, as an adult, yeah.' and ongoing asthma discussion.
History of hay fever: 'Yes, I had asthma. I also had hay fever and asthma eczema as well.' and later: 'Any other medical problems?' 'I have hay fever as well.'
History of eczema: 'Yes, I had asthma. I also had hay fever and asthma eczema as well.'
Past hospital visits for asthma: 'And did you ever have to go to hospital with it?' 'Yeah, sometimes.'
No ICU admissions: 'Did you ever get severely unwell, have to be on intensive care unit or anything like that?' 'No, not that bad. But still sometimes need to go to hospital...'
Use of salbutamol inhaler every few weeks: 'Have you taken any medication?' 'I took sulbutomal. Yeah.' 'And how often do you normally need it?' 'Every few weeks. I'm not sure.'
No drug allergies reported: 'Any allergies to medications?' 'No, no allergies.'
Lives with partner: 'Who do you live with? Do you live on your own or do you live with.' 'I live with my partner.'
Occupation engineer: 'And what's your job day to day?' 'I'm an engineer.'
Non-smoker: 'Do you smoke?' 'No, I don't smoke.'
Alcohol intake: 'Do you drink any alcohol regularly?' 'Yeah, one glass.' 'How often? One glass of what?' 'One glass of wine every.' 'How often did you say?' 'Every two or three days. Depends. Yeah.'
Self-reported temperature: 'Did you say you checked your temperature already?' 'Yes, I checked.' 'Was it normal?' 'Yeah, yeah.' 'What Was your temperature?' '37. Yeah.'
No other vitals or physical examination findings are discussed anywhere in the transcript, so stating they are not documented is accurate.
'It sounds like you've had a flare up of your asthma.' is said after history of asthma plus 2–3 days of SOB and cough, matching assessment of acute asthma exacerbation.

Clinician links hay fever/allergy as contributor: 'It could be triggered by if there's more pollen around or there may be. You may have a viral infection...' and later recommends antihistamine for hay fever, indicating allergic rhinitis as relevant comorbidity.

Plan for peak flow meter and monitoring: 'I can prescribe you a peak flow meter so we can check your breathing level' and 'if you could record a value first thing when you wake up in the evening over the next week.' (morning and evening for a week).
Spacer prescription: 'I can prescribe you... a spacer to use your inhaler a bit more efficiently.'
Pharmacist demonstration: 'which the pharmacist can show you how you use that when you pick it up' and 'The pharmacist can show you how to use it' referring to spacer and peak flow.
Increased SABA usage: 'if you increase it so you're taking it two to four puffs, like every four hours initially...' referring to asthma inhaler (salbutamol already identified).

Antihistamine recommendation with note: 'And the other thing to do would be to take a regular antihistamine, which you can get from the pharmacy. I can put a suggestion on your notes about what to take.'

Clinician advises urgent review if high temperature or worsening wheeze: 'if you get a high temperature or your wheezing is getting worse, you need to call us back straight away.' There is no mention of advice specifically about 'unable to speak in sentences' or other broader concerning signs.

Follow-up in about a week to reassess asthma/peak flow: 'it would be a good idea, when you're feeling better, if we could arrange just a review...' and 'You can arrange a review in a week or so.' plus discussion of reviewing peak flow readings next week.
Earlier contact if fever or wheeze worsens: 'if you get a high temperature or your wheezing is getting worse, you need to call us back straight away.'
